correctness.rationale: For irreducible reversible stochastic W the D^1/2 W D^-1/2 similarity is symmetric with stationary projection 1*pi^T. Derive finite peer epoch multiplier (1-alpha+alpha^(K+1)*mu^K*(1-mu))/(1-alpha*mu): denominator >0, for mu>=0 always positive; even K strictly positive for all mu; odd K exactly one possible negative root. Each epoch kills at most one distinct negative nonconstant eigenvalue, so generic initial vectors require at least their number of epochs, regardless of adaptive choices. K=1 and alpha=1/(1-mu) constructs the exact projection when all nonconstant eigenvalues are negative. Reversible nonedge implies principal 2x2 matrix diagonal and mu_2>=min W_uu,W_vv>=0 via interlacing; for simple regular graphs only complete graph qualifies. Independent three-state exact Fraction calculation annihilates two distinct negative eigenvalues and produces J/3. Strong statement is restricted to fixed W, shared scalar alpha in (0,1), finite K and anchor resetting; generic-input lower bound is not a uniform bound over every degenerate initial vector.
